items.title: Sugar-Free Fries & Other Lies
items.summary: STOP PROMOTING UR SUGAR-FREE FRIES AND KETO YOGURTS. The wellness craze in…
items.content_html:
STOP PROMOTING UR SUGAR-FREE FRIES AND KETO YOGURTS.

The wellness craze in Lebanon is out of control. Around summer 2024 with a PEAK in spring 2025, suddenly there were healthy collagen smoothie places and random pilates studios at every street corner. I am not talking about Backburner (it has always been there, but boy did it get turned into an overpriced “to-be-seen” spot overnight). I am talking more specifically about places like The Glow Paradise. There are endless places like it, but their marketing really pisses me off because they sell this total illusion of health to young girls

Again, I am not solely referring to the quality or source of their products (at that price, I pray to GOD they are good, though I’d love to see the actual farm names for this local “grass-fed beef” in Lebanon, because IT IS THOSE farmers who deserve real recognition after the crisis). I am looking at the 3-digit label right next to every marvelously named food item on their menu: the calorie count.

How MANY TIMES have I stumbled on videos of influencers my age and older trying the Glow matcha that “only has 120 kcal guys”!!!!! It exasperates me. One, because these girls usually have absolutely no clue what the hell they are talking about. They scan their meals every day with an AI calorie counter app, then complain to their followers about having a piece of cake. I am not attacking those girls. But as someone who has suffered with an eating disorder, I can't sit and watch people PROMOTING that kind of stuff to others. If someone is struggling, I hope from the bottom of my heart that you have the support you need, but please save that for tumblr thinspo and not the FYP of a random tween who has never even heard of calories before.

Also, it is incredibly interesting how these “healthful” foods are systematically marketed to women. Look at their posts: women in bikinis or tight little Alo Yoga sets (note: funny how Western activewear branding is increasingly pushing Eurocentric body standards onto Arab women), talking about “youthful face,” “rejuvenation,” and “game changer for skin health.” They sell anti-aging to a clientele made of teens and young adults. Helloo???? What about ESSENTIAL health?

It blows my mind how our society treats a woman’s physical appearance as “health” instead of her internal organ function. Obviously one follows the other: if your body is operating right internally, the rest shows. But if young girls end up chronically undereating because they are terrified of calories, believe me, their fertility, bone density, and actual hair health will be completely wrecked. No amount of collagen powder saves your endocrine system when you are running a massive calorie deficit lol. Posting those hyper-curated bodies sets extremely unrealistic expectations, especially for Arab girls. I am not generalizing, but from actual experience, observation, and scientific truth, Arab female physiognomy (fat distribution, bone structures…)is just naturally, BIOLOGICLLY, different from those white French sticks! And they keep using words like nourish, nourish, nourish. Like they even have weight loss plans lol. I don't know how they interact with those clients, but I really hope they inform them properly instead of throwing them into a giant orthorexia pit.

(Uhm, so side note: I realized I keep saying ”they.” When I say “they,” I mean The Glow Paradise. But let's be real this predatory pattern exists everywhere in the world,not just Beirut)

ALSO, I am not saying people should be completely oblivious to the energetic values of what they ingest! I would be a crazy person and healthcare worker if I discouraged basic nutritional literacy. Take the US or Canada, if there was no nutritional info on menus, people would spend their whole daily energy expenditure on one peameal bacon bagel. So we need to educate people in a realistic and scientific way!

Yes, whole foods are best for our bodies. Yes, everything is processed nowadays. But surprise surprise, whole foods today are ALSO processed. So when you spend $11 on four pieces of organic chicken nuggets, each the size of my thumb, or a sad little omelette, you are 1. wasting money and 2. missing the actual experience of going out to eat. You can make all of that at home for a quarter of the price. Stop being so gullible to aesthetic pastel colored pretty plates and the vibe of a place just to avoid looking at what you are actually ingesting. (If you want an example of a spot actually doing healthful food right, look at places like Honest Greens).

The best thing in my and EXPERTS' opinion (it should be standard advice, really) is to eat healthy at home. And by HEALTHY, I mean eat the rainbow, avoid processed dairy products or heavy store-bought dressings, ditch the zero-sugar carbonated drinks (the chemical additives damage ur gut microbiome)… Then, when you TREAT yourself by going out, have something you CANNOT cook at home. We have normalized eating out so much today when it used to be a luxury!

All this to say: before getting sucked into the goop-flavored black hole of wellness aesthetic, please educate yourself, and please please please be careful with what you consume online. If you are ever in need of support, please reach out to your loved ones. I never want anyone to feel like they aren't good enough. Love yourself and be kind to others.

items.title: La Gazelle de Waller
items.summary: Imaginez la personne la plus chic, la plus discrète et la plus…
items.content_html:
Imaginez la personne la plus chic, la plus discrète et la plus cultivée que vous puissiez croiser : c'est exactement ce que j'appelle une Gazelle de Waller. J'ai tenu à ce que ma toute première publication ici soit consacrée à ce concept parce qu'il me semble indispensable que mes lecteurs et lectrices observent le monde à travers cette grille de lecture, ne serait-ce que pour saisir le fil conducteur de mes prochains posts.

Bon, retour à notre sujet. Une Gazelle de Waller, c’est quelqu’un qui n’a absolument rien à prouver (when ykyk). C'est le produit d'un confort générationnel familial qui dépasse les simples critères financiers "d'aisance". Elle doit venir d'une famille éduquée respectable qui a de bonnes valeurs et toujours attachée à ses traditions.

Chez la Gazelle de Waller, le luxe n'a rien d'ostentatoire. Puisque, justement, elle a grandi dans un environnement raffiné, pour elle, c'est tout à fait normal d'être entourée de ce qu'il y'a de mieux. Alors quand je parle de luxe, je ne fais évidemment PAS référence aux it-bags de la saison, à la logomania ou à tout ce qui crie sa marque à dix mètres (l'horreur absolue). Je fais plutôt référence à choisir systématiquement ce qu’il y a de plus noble comme matière sans jamais opter pour ce qui est facilement identifiable (qu'il s'agisse d'un cuir de veau Box pleine fleur, d'une pure vigogne, ou d'une soie grège brute). Bref, le savoir-faire et la durabilité priment sur tout le reste.

Cette même exigence se retrouve dans son rapport aux autres. La bienséance et l'étiquette chez la Gazelle de Waller sont instinctivement intégrées. Elle sait où aller, comment se comporter, quoi dire, quand se taire. On peut aussi bien la croiser emmitouflée dans un manteau vintage seconde-main au lobby d'un grand hôtel parisien qu'attablée le lendemain sur un tabouret en plastique au cœur d'une médina, un thé à la menthe à la main. Tout cela bien évidemment sans perdre sa confiance et sa noblesse. 

Son érudition ferait pâlir les théories de Bourdieu sur le capital culturel : elle comprend l'art, la haute parfumerie, la gastronomie, les matières et la littérature... Même en voyage, la quête d'authenticité prend le dessus sur les adresses trendy de la saison. Elle préfère une petite table dénichée au coin d'une ruelle plutôt qu'un resto où tout le monde se presse et fait la queue.

Dans son univers discret (qu'il ne faudrait SURTOUT pas le confondre avec de l'hésitation ou de la timidité) chaque détail autour d'elle est minutieusement observé. On pourrait facilement passer à côté d'une Gazelle de Waller sur le trottoir sans y prêter attention, mais pour quiconque sait vraiment observer, sa présence finit toujours par triompher.

P.S. Pourquoi ce nom ? Parce que la Gazelle de Waller  (aussi connu sous le nom de Gérénuk) est sans doute l'animal rare le plus absurdement élégant de la savane, ne vivant qu'en très petit groupe. Considérez désormais ce blog comme leur point de ralliement.

P.S. 2 : La vraie Gazelle de Waller, c'est ma Mima (et ses sœurs).

items.title: Helloes, to the Habibis
items.summary: Alors. This "blog" (or whatever you want to call it) is entirely…
items.content_html:
Alors. 

This "blog" (or whatever you want to call it) is entirely dedicated to my opinion.

I’m taking my EYE 🧿 to profile people (and normal civilians too). I sit down with them and ask observational NON-boring questions instead of basic PR ones. 

Oh and I'm also dumping my notebook entries here. I'm planning on writing micro-essays on the design behind IKEA’s winding paths, consumerism, CAN Ibiza, the disappearance of newsstands on Toronto sidewalks, hotel concierges (Mr. Gustave my icon), organic toilet paper, Hermès Horizon’s... all of it.

Plus I’m an HBSc candidate so I'm also thinking of translating and dumping down info I read in dense research papers on the gut microbiome (an area of personal interest) into stuff you can actually read without falling asleep.

I know this sounds all over the place. I'll get better at writing don't worry lol.

Consider this your MASTERCLASS on how to become a true GAZELLE DE WALLER. Pure taste and high cultural capital.

Read along. Or don't, habibi.
